data.content:
indication,screening	Confrontation test
Visual field impairment
The confrontation test is used to screen for visual field defects only when there is no clinical indication of such impairment or a progressive eye condition.

evaluation,requirement	Formal perimetry-based assessment
Visual field defect
Any person with a visual field defect or suspected of having one must undergo a formal perimetry-based assessment.

baseline,standard	Monocular automated static perimetry
Visual field assessments
This method serves as the minimum baseline standard for visual field assessments; if it shows no defect, the standard is confirmed.

assessment,requirement	Binocular Esterman visual field
Significant field defect
Subjects with a significant field defect or progressive eye condition require a binocular Esterman visual field for assessment.

administration,device	Binocular Esterman visual field
Humphrey visual field analyser
The Humphrey visual field analyser is classically used to administer the binocular Esterman visual field test.

alternative,equivalence	Binocular Esterman visual field
Medmont binocular VF
The Medmont binocular VF is an accepted alternative device that can produce results equivalent to the standard Esterman chart.

determination,testing protocol	Corrective lenses
Treating optometrist
The treating optometrist determines whether it is appropriate for a person to wear their normal corrective lenses during testing.

determination,testing protocol	Corrective lenses
Treating ophthalmologist
The treating ophthalmologist determines whether it is appropriate for a person to wear their normal corrective lenses during testing.

recording,requirement	Fixation monitoring
Test
Fixation monitoring must be performed and recorded on the test to ensure validity.

capability,requirement	Alternative devices
Fixation monitoring
Alternative devices must have the ability to monitor fixation in order to be considered for use.

reliability,threshold	Esterman binocular chart
False-positive score
For an Esterman binocular chart to be considered reliable for licensing, the false-positive score must not exceed 20 per cent.

fitness,restriction,safety	Diplopia
Driving
Individuals suffering from diplopia are generally not fit to drive due to the condition's impact on visual safety.

assessment,referral	Diplopia
Optometrist
People suspected of experiencing diplopia should be referred for assessment by an optometrist.

assessment,referral	Diplopia
Ophthalmologist
People suspected of experiencing diplopia should be referred for assessment by an ophthalmologist.

re-establishment,recovery	Depth Perception
Occluder
When diplopia is managed with an occluder, depth perception must be re-established over a three-month period.

prohibition,restriction	Driving
Occluder
A three-month non-driving period applies when diplopia is managed with an occluder to ensure safety before resuming driving.

eligibility,fitness,visual defects	Commercial Standards
Unconditional Licence
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence if they have any visual field defect.

assessment,consideration,criteria,granting,issuance,licensing,medical condition,period,regulation,review	Conditional Licence
Driver Licensing Authority
The authority may consider a conditional licence subject to annual review based on information from treating optometrists or ophthalmologists.<SEP>For a conditional licence based on monocular vision, the authority reviews the case subject to a 2-yearly review.<SEP>The driver licensing authority grants conditional licences while taking into account the nature of the driving task and the medical condition.<SEP>The authority considers granting a conditional license subject to periodic review if the driver meets vision standards with corrective lenses.<SEP>The authority considers issuing the licence based on specific criteria and reviews it annually.<SEP>The driver licensing authority considers a conditional licence subject to 2-yearly review.

assessment,criteria,information,medical input,visual field	Conditional Licence
Treating Optometrist
The optometrist provides information regarding the nature of the driving task and visual criteria to the licensing authority.<SEP>The optometrist provides data regarding the driver's visual field to inform the licensing decision.<SEP>A treating optometrist provides information regarding visual acuity and field to support the consideration of a conditional licence.

assessment,information,visual field	Conditional Licence
Treating Ophthalmologist
The ophthalmologist provides information regarding the nature of the driving task and visual criteria to the licensing authority.

criteria,extent,measurement,midline,requirement	Binocular Visual Field
Conditional Licence
For a binocular visual field to meet conditional licence criteria, it must have an extent of at least 140 degrees within 10 degrees above and below the horizontal midline.<SEP>A minimum extent of at least 140 degrees within 10 degrees above and below the horizontal midline is a required criterion for the licence.

criteria,hemianopia,performance,quadrantanopia,remaining eye,scotoma	Conditional Licence
Significant Visual Field Loss
A person is not fit for a conditional licence if they have significant visual field loss (such as scotoma, hemianopia, or quadrantanopia) likely to impede driving performance.<SEP>For a conditional licence based on monocular vision, there must be no other significant visual field loss likely to impede driving performance.

criteria,eligibility,fitness	Monocular Vision
Unconditional Licence
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence if they are monocular.

criteria,progression,stability,static	Conditional Licence
Visual Field Loss
For a conditional licence based on binocular vision, the visual field loss must be static and unlikely to progress rapidly.<SEP>The visual field loss must be static and unlikely to progress rapidly to qualify for the licence.

correction,criteria,remaining eye,requirement,vision	Conditional Licence
Visual Acuity
For a conditional licence based on monocular vision, the visual acuity in the remaining eye must be 6/9 or better with or without correction.<SEP>A conditional licence requires visual acuity in the remaining eye to be 6/9 or better with or without correction.

criteria,horizontal extent,midline,remaining eye,requirement,vision	Conditional Licence
Visual Field
For a conditional licence based on monocular vision, the visual field in the remaining eye must have a horizontal extent of at least 140 degrees within 10 degrees above and below the horizontal midline.<SEP>A conditional licence requires visual field in the remaining eye to have a horizontal extent of at least 140 degrees within 10 degrees above and below the horizontal midline.

driving,eligibility,fitness,limits,visual acuity	Commercial standards
Unconditional licence
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence if they experience diplopia within 20 degrees from central fixation.<SEP>A person is not fit to hold an unconditional licence if their uncorrected visual acuity exceeds specific thresholds in either eye.

corrective lenses,driving,eligibility,fitness,review	Commercial standards
Conditional licence
A person is not fit to hold a conditional licence if they experience diplopia within 20 degrees from central fixation.<SEP>A conditional licence may be considered by the driver licensing authority if the visual standard is met with corrective lenses or under specific vision conditions.

disqualification,visual impairment	Commercial standards
Diplopia
Experiencing diplopia (other than physiological diplopia) within 20 degrees from central fixation is a criterion for determining if a person is not fit to hold certain licences.

exclusion,normal vision	Diplopia
Physiological diplopia
Physiological diplopia is excluded from the definition of diplopia that renders a person unfit to hold a licence.

equipment,therapy,usage	Orthokeratology
Rigid Gas-Permeable Contact Lenses
Orthokeratology involves the therapeutic use of rigid gas-permeable contact lenses worn overnight.

effect,procedure,target	Cornea
Orthokeratology
Orthokeratology is used to reshape the cornea of the eye through the application of contact lenses.

correction,outcome,treatment	Orthokeratology
Visual Refractive Error
Orthokeratology provides effective correction of visual refractive error that can last at least a full day once the lenses are removed.

condition,permission,requirement	Conditional Licence
Private Vehicle Drivers
A conditional licence can be considered for private vehicle drivers provided they meet visual acuity standards with orthokeratology therapy.

condition,permission,requirement	Commercial Vehicle Drivers
Conditional Licence
A conditional licence can be considered for commercial vehicle drivers provided they meet visual acuity standards with orthokeratology therapy.

authorization,guidance,recommendation	Conditional Licence
Optometrist
A conditional licence is granted based on recommendations from an optometrist regarding lens wear.

assessment,authorization,criteria,guidance,information,medical input,recommendation	Conditional Licence
Ophthalmologist
A conditional licence is granted based on recommendations from an ophthalmologist regarding lens wear.<SEP>The ophthalmologist provides data regarding the driver's visual field to inform the licensing decision.<SEP>An ophthalmologist provides information regarding visual acuity and field to support the consideration of a conditional licence.

exceptional cases,medical assessment,referral	Driver Licensing Authority
Medical Specialist Opinion
The Driver Licensing Authority refers cases to medical specialists for opinion in unusual circumstances.

independent experts,panels,reference	Driver Licensing Authority
Part A section 3.3.7
The Driver Licensing Authority's referral process is referenced in Part A section 3.3.7 regarding the role of independent experts and panels.

maintenance,support	Orthokeratology Therapy
Visual Acuity Standard
The therapy provides the necessary support to maintain the established visual acuity standard.

correction,enable	Correcting Lenses
Visual Acuity Standard
These lenses enable individuals to meet the visual acuity standard when other methods are not sufficient.

cancellation,issuance,renewal,suspension	Driver Licence
Driver Licensing Authority
The Driver Licensing Authority holds ultimate responsibility for the issuance, renewal, suspension, or cancellation of a driver licence.

information provision,medical criteria	Driver Licensing Authority
Health Professional
The Health Professional provides details of unmet medical criteria, evidence of met criteria, and proposed conditions to the Driver Licensing Authority.

issuance requirement,monitoring	Conditional Licence
Health Professional
The Health Professional must provide specific medical details for a Conditional Licence to be issued.

concurrent conditions,impact	Fitness to Drive
Hearing Impairment
Hearing impairment may combine with other medical conditions to affect fitness to drive.

concurrent conditions,impact	Fitness to Drive
Visual Impairment
Visual impairment may combine with other medical conditions to affect fitness to drive.

concurrent conditions,impact	Cognitive Impairment
Fitness to Drive
Cognitive impairment may combine with other medical conditions to affect fitness to drive.

assessment,referral,vision	Optometrist
Visual Acuity
An optometrist may refer a person for further assessment if the person does not meet visual acuity standards.

assessment,referral,vision	Ophthalmologist
Visual Acuity
An ophthalmologist may refer a person for further assessment if the person does not meet visual acuity standards.

fitness to drive,regulation,safety	Nystagmus
Visual Acuity Standard
Drivers with nystagmus must meet the visual acuity standard to ensure safety on the road.

assessment,evaluation,medical review	Appropriate Specialist
Nystagmus
Individuals with nystagmus should be assessed by an appropriate specialist to determine fitness to drive.

assessment,coping strategies,individual evaluation	Appropriate Specialist
Congenital Nystagmus
Those with congenital nystagmus may have developed coping strategies and require individual assessment by a specialist.

association,evidence,safety	Motor Vehicle Crash Risk
Visual Fields
There is an incomplete relationship between visual fields and crash risk, as the evidence regarding this association is limited.

correlation,driving safety,impairment	Motor Vehicle Crash Risk
Visual Acuity
Reduced visual acuity is associated with an increased risk of motor vehicle crashes, although identifying the exact degree of this increase is challenging.

criteria,drivers,measurement	Licensing Standards
Visual Acuity
Evidence regarding visual acuity impairment is generally limited to drivers who already meet licensing standards, restricting the ability to determine if alternative cut-points are more appropriate.

colour vision,laboratory testing,red lights	Motor Vehicle Crash Risk
Red Colour-Deficient Vision
Research suggests there is no general association between crash risk and colour vision, though individuals with red-colour-deficient vision have difficulty detecting red lights in laboratory and on-road testing.

compensation,driving capability,engineering improvements	Red Colour-Deficient Vision
Road Engineering
Significant improvements in road engineering mean that people with red-colour-deficient vision may largely compensate for their deficiency while driving.

assessment,granting,review	Conditional licence
Driver licensing authority
The driver licensing authority evaluates and considers a conditional licence subject to periodic review based on visual standards.

assessment,certification,measurement	Treating optometrist
Visual acuity
The treating optometrist provides the visual acuity measurements required to determine if a person meets the standard for a conditional licence.

assessment,certification,measurement	Ophthalmologist
Visual acuity
The ophthalmologist provides the visual acuity measurements required to determine if a person meets the standard for a conditional licence.

information,reference,standards	Driver licensing authority
Orthokeratology therapy
The driver licensing authority refers to Orthokeratology therapy for information on meeting the visual standard using this specific treatment.

extension,visual field defect	Central Loss
Hemianopia
Central loss is defined as an extension of hemianopia or quadrantanopia.

extension,visual field defect	Central Loss
Quadrantanopia
Central loss is defined as an extension of hemianopia or quadrantanopia.

assessment,demands	Driver Licensing Authority
Real-World Driving Environment
The driver licensing authority considers the demands of the real-world driving environment when assessing patients with visual field defects.

assessment,measurement method	Driver Licensing Authority
Kinetic Fields
Kinetic fields conducted on a Goldman are additional factors considered by the driver licensing authority.

assessment,measurement method	Driver Licensing Authority
Esterman Visual Fields
Binocular Esterman visual fields conducted without fixation monitoring are additional factors considered by the driver licensing authority.

assessment factor	Contrast Sensitivity
Driver Licensing Authority
Contrast sensitivity is an additional factor to be considered by the driver licensing authority.

assessment factor	Driver Licensing Authority
Glare Susceptibility
Glare susceptibility is an additional factor to be considered by the driver licensing authority.

assessment factor,prognosis	Driver Licensing Authority
Medical History
Medical history including duration, prognosis, progression rate, and treatment effectiveness is an additional factor to be considered by the driver licensing authority.

assessment factor,history	Driver Licensing Authority
Driving Record
The driving record before and since the occurrence of a defect is an additional factor to be considered by the driver licensing authority.

assessment factor,conditions	Driver Licensing Authority
Nature of Driving Task
The nature of the driving task including vehicle type and concomitant medical conditions is an additional factor to be considered by the driver licensing authority.

assessment,restriction	Commercial Vehicle Drivers
Monocular Vision
There is no flexibility for commercial vehicle drivers regarding monocular vision and its associated visual field reductions.

definition,measurement	Normal visual field
Visual fields
Defines the extent of normal peripheral vision in terms of degrees in different directions.

extension,stereopsis	Binocular field
Visual fields
Extends the horizontal visual range and provides overlapping central vision for depth perception.

neurological condition,reduction	Stroke
Visual fields
A neurological condition that can cause a reduction in the extent of visual fields.

neurological condition,reduction	Multiple sclerosis
Visual fields
A neurological condition that can cause a reduction in the extent of visual fields.

ocular disease,reduction	Glaucoma
Visual fields
An ocular disease that can cause a reduction in the extent of visual fields.

injury,reduction type	Hemionopia
Visual fields
A specific type of visual field loss resulting from neurological conditions or injuries.

injury,reduction type	Quadrantanopia
Visual fields
A specific type of visual field loss resulting from neurological conditions or injuries.

injury,reduction type	Monocularity
Visual fields
A specific type of visual field loss resulting from neurological conditions or injuries.

awareness,environment	Driver
Peripheral vision
Assists the driver in being aware of the total driving environment before central focus is applied.

assessment,conditional licence	Optometrist
Visual fields
Assesses longstanding field defects to determine if a conditional licence should be considered.

adaptation,safety	Driver
Peripheral vision loss
Incomplete peripheral vision loss allows awareness through adaptation, while full impairment decreases safety.

assessment,conditional licence	Ophthalmologist
Visual fields
Assesses longstanding field defects to determine if a conditional licence should be considered.

adaptation,management	Conditional licence
Visual fields
Requires assessment of visual field defects and evidence of visual adaptation for management as an exceptional case.

commercial vehicle,heavy vehicle,licence status	Conditional Licence
Farmer
A farmer requiring a commercial vehicle licence for occasional use of a heavy vehicle may have a different licence status compared to other drivers.

driving task,licence status	Conditional Licence
Interstate Multiple Combination Vehicle Driver
An interstate multiple combination vehicle driver has a licence status that is quite different from that of a farmer.

advice,examination,medical condition	Driver Licensing Authority
Examining Health Professional
The examining health professional provides advice to the driver licensing authority when examining a person and considering their medical condition.

driving effects,legal obligation,notification	Driver Licensing Authority
Patient
Patients have a legal obligation to notify the driver licensing authority where driving is likely to be affected by their condition.

advice,awareness,effects of condition	Examining Health Professional
Patient
The examining health professional advises patients about the effects of their condition on driving and their legal obligations.

assessment,limitations,reliability	Disorders of Vision
Practical Driver Assessment
The practical driver assessment is not considered a safe or reliable method for assessing the effects of disorders of vision on driving.

assessment,limitations	Practical Driver Assessment
Visual Fields
The practical driver assessment is not considered a safe or reliable method for assessing the effects of disorders of vision on visual fields.

determination,response	Emergency Situations
Practical Driver Assessment
The driver's response to emergency situations cannot be determined through practical driver assessments.

determination,response	Environmental Conditions
Practical Driver Assessment
The driver's response to various environmental conditions cannot be determined through practical driver assessments.

adaptation,information	Disorders of Vision
Visual Field Tests
Information about adaptation to visual field defects can be gained from visual field tests.

ability,assessment	Practical Driver Assessment
Visual Information Processing
A practical driver assessment may be helpful in assessing the ability to process visual information.

ability,impact,restriction	Driving
Progressive Eye Conditions
Progressive eye conditions may result in future restrictions on driving due to their potential impact on visual ability.

advice,diagnosis,monitoring	Patient
Progressive Eye Conditions
Patients diagnosed with progressive eye conditions should be monitored regularly and advised in advance about potential impacts.

adaptation,engagement,preparation	Blindness and Low Vision Services
Patient
Patients are advised to prepare for changes by potentially engaging with blindness and low vision services.

Driving,Essential,Safety	Motor Vehicle Operation
Vision
Good vision is essential for operating a motor vehicle safely.

Diminish,Hazardous,Perception	Driving Ability
Eye Disorders
Marked loss of visual acuity or visual fields diminishes a person's ability to drive safely and detect hazards.

Awareness,Detection,Side Vision	Driving Environment Awareness
Peripheral Vision
Peripheral vision assists drivers in being aware of the total driving environment and detecting objects to the side.

Reduced Abilities,Slow Development,Unawareness	Driver Awareness
Vision Defects
Vision defects can develop slowly, causing drivers to be unaware of their reduced abilities, particularly in relation to peripheral vision.

Detection,Pedestrians,Signs,Vehicles	Hazard Detection
Visual Acuity Loss
Loss of visual acuity reduces the ability to detect other vehicles, pedestrians, and warning signs.

biological process,decline	Ageing
Vision
Vision is associated with the natural process of ageing, leading to a decline in visual acuity.

assessment,safety	Fitness to Drive
Vision
The state of vision is a critical consideration when assessing an individual's fitness to drive.

age-related,decline	Older People
Vision
In older people, the decline in vision is an important factor considered for driving safety.

assessment,factors	Fitness to Drive
Older People
For older people, fitness to drive involves considerations of vision alongside cognition and sensory-motor function.

condition,prevalence	Cataracts
Older People
Cataracts are a progressive eye condition that is more common in older people.

condition,prevalence	Glaucoma
Older People
Glaucoma is a progressive eye condition that is more common in older people.

condition,prevalence	Macular Degeneration
Older People
Macular degeneration is a progressive eye condition that is more common in older people.

management,monitoring	Cataracts
Conditional Licences
Once diagnosed, cataracts require regular monitoring in relation to driving, potentially involving conditional licences.

management,monitoring	Conditional Licences
Glaucoma
Once diagnosed, glaucoma requires regular monitoring in relation to driving, potentially involving conditional licences.

management,monitoring	Conditional Licences
Macular Degeneration
Once diagnosed, macular degeneration requires regular monitoring in relation to driving, potentially involving conditional licences.

complication,screening	Diabetes
Retinopathy
Diabetes requires monitoring to screen for and manage end-organ effects such as retinopathy.

assessment,outcome	Fitness to Drive
Stroke
For drivers with stroke, vision is one of the functional outcomes addressed in an overall assessment of fitness to drive.

assessment,integration	Fitness to Drive
Neurological Conditions
Findings related to neurological conditions such as stroke are integrated as part of the overall assessment for fitness to drive.

assessment focus,vision aspects	Visual Acuity
Visual Fields
Both visual acuity and visual fields are identified as the two main aspects of vision addressed in the chapter.

health impact,medical criteria	Neurological Conditions
Vision
Neurological conditions are cited as a category of conditions that may affect vision.

health impact,medical criteria	Diabetes Mellitus
Vision
Diabetes mellitus is cited as a condition that may affect vision.

age-related changes,management approach	Older Drivers
Vision
Age-related changes in older drivers are noted as a factor affecting vision.

advice,deficiency,medical guidance	Doctors
Drivers
Medical professionals should advise drivers who have significant color vision deficiency about the impact on their driving.

adaptation,advice,visual impairment	Drivers
Optometrists
Eye care specialists should inform drivers regarding how color vision deficiency affects responsiveness to signal lights and the need for driving adaptations.

adaptation,advice,visual impairment	Drivers
Ophthalmologists
Eye specialists should advise drivers on how color vision deficiency impacts their ability to respond to signal lights and the necessity of adapting their driving.

perception,responsiveness,traffic signals	Drivers
Signal Lights
Drivers must respond to signal lights, a task that can be affected by significant color vision deficiency.

absence,requirement,standard	Colour Vision
Drivers
There is currently no established standard for colour vision requirements applicable to drivers in either private or commercial contexts.

applicability,limitation,scope	Colour Vision
Normal Road Rules and Conditions
The existing driving standards regarding colour vision apply exclusively to driving within normal road rules and conditions.

assessment,justification,task-specific	Colour Vision
Risk Assessment
A standard requiring colour vision may be justified through risk assessment for particular driving tasks.

criteria,disqualification,eligibility,fitness,qualification,restriction,visual health	Person
Unconditional Licence
A person is deemed unfit to hold an unconditional licence if their visual acuity fails to meet specific standards.<SEP>A person is not eligible to hold an unconditional licence if they have a visual field defect.<SEP>A person is not eligible to hold an unconditional licence if they experience diplopia within a specific visual field range.

assessment,condition,measurement	Person
Visual Acuity
The fitness of a person to hold the licence is determined by measuring their uncorrected visual acuity.

restriction,standard,threshold	Six over Nine
Unconditional Licence
Holding an unconditional licence requires that the person's uncorrected visual acuity in the better eye not be worse than 6/9.

restriction,standard,threshold	Six over Eighteen
Unconditional Licence
Holding an unconditional licence requires that the person's uncorrected visual acuity in either eye not be worse than 6/18.

assessment,criteria,evaluation	Driver Licensing Authority
Vision
The authority evaluates visual acuity, specifically requiring 6/9 in the better eye or worse than 6/18 in the worse eye.

assessment,certification,measurement	Treating Optometrist
Vision
The optometrist provides the visual acuity data required by the authority to determine license eligibility.

assessment,certification,measurement	Ophthalmologist
Vision
The ophthalmologist provides the visual acuity data required by the authority to determine license eligibility.

correction,improvement,standard	Corrective Lenses
Vision
Corrective lenses are used to improve vision to meet the specific acuity standards required for a conditional license.

correction,improvement,standard	Orthokeratology Therapy
Vision
This therapy is referenced as a method to meet the visual standard using corrective lenses for a conditional license.

consideration,nature,restriction	Driver Licensing Authority
Driving Task
The authority takes into account the nature of the driving task when evaluating applicants.

consideration,nature,restriction	Driver Licensing Authority
Underlying Disorder
The authority considers the nature of any underlying disorder affecting the applicant's vision.

criteria,exclusion,impairment	Conditional Licence
Scotoma
The presence of significant visual field loss such as a scotoma that impedes driving performance is a criterion for denying the licence.

criteria,exclusion,impairment	Conditional Licence
Hemianopia
The presence of significant visual field loss such as hemianopia that impedes driving performance is a criterion for denying the licence.

criteria,exclusion,impairment	Conditional Licence
Quadrantanopia
The presence of significant visual field loss such as quadrantanopia that impedes driving performance is a criterion for denying the licence.

driving licence,eligibility,fitness	Monocular Person
Unconditional Licence
A person who is monocular is not fit to hold an unconditional licence.

impediment,risk,safety	Driving Performance
Significant Visual Field Loss
Significant visual field loss that is likely to impede driving performance disqualifies a person from holding a conditional licence.

fitness,qualification,restriction	Conditional Licence
Person
A person is not eligible to hold a conditional licence if they experience diplopia within a specific visual field range.

classification,exception,exclusion	Diplopia
Physiological Diplopia
The condition of experiencing diplopia is relevant to licence fitness unless it is classified as physiological diplopia.

measurement,range,visual field	Central Fixation
Diplopia
The assessment of diplopia involves measuring its presence within 20 degrees from the point of central fixation.
